findings.title: Raw substring matching applies upsampling to non-error Discover queries
findings.body: The Discover eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. Valid queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `!event.type:error`, or a quoted search term containing that text therefore have `count()` replaced with `upsampled_count()`. Those queries can include transaction/non-error rows, for which this code explicitly says `sample_weight` is not available, producing invalid queries or incorrect totals. Determine event-type eligibility from the parsed query and require that the query is semantically restricted to errors rather than using a substring check.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the original dataset instead of the executed dataset
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but passes the outer `dataset` closure to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard split flow, the original metrics-enhanced request invokes `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query)` for the error portion, while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper rejects metrics datasets, so these actual error queries never receive upsampled counts. Eligibility needs to use the dataset/query being executed (and, for split queries, the split query rather than only the original request parameters).

findings.title: The internal upsampled aggregation is exposed without the allowlist guard
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is registered as a normal public SnQL function, unlike the adjacent internal aggregation marked `private=True`. A caller can submit `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly to a Discover/events-stats query for unallowlisted projects or transaction data, bypassing `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and getting an invalid or misleading aggregate. Mark this function private or enforce the same project/dataset validation at the resolver boundary.

findings.title: The PR adds an unrelated nested-repository gitlink
findings.body: This adds a `sentry-repo` subproject entry pinned to the base commit, despite the feature not requiring a submodule and without any accompanying submodule configuration change. Fresh or recursive checkouts will treat this path as a nested repository dependency rather than normal source content, potentially failing to initialize it or needlessly cloning another repository. Remove the gitlink unless this is an intentional, properly declared submodule dependency.
